Minerals and Metals Working Group, Climate Change Industry Issues Table and The Canadian Lime Institute (1999). Industrial Minerals Options Paper. National Climate Change Process, Ottawa, October 1999. No report number, DOI or URL printed.

Locators are printed page numbers (equal to PDF pages). The paper covers only the Canadian merchant lime industry. Main file: two technologies - the new higher-efficiency 350 t/day kiln assumed in the replacement action (capacity, utilisation, life, 6.0 GJ/t, capex $15-25M 1999 CAD with a derived per t/yr value, process and derived combustion CO2) and the industry-average kiln (6.6 GJ/t, 0.69 t CO2e/t combustion factor, 0.79 t/t process CO2). The kiln type of the new kiln is not stated, so mapping is low. Measures: the two analysed actions (kiln replacement, operator training) and the I.D.-fan rule of thumb. Other-values: Table 1 emissions series, Appendix A sector emissions, electricity use, energy cost, re-absorption figures. Not loaded: Appendix B non-analysed actions (no numbers). No kiln_lime-oxy-fuel data (oxy-fuel not mentioned). Traps: printed throughput 102,000 t vs arithmetic 102,200; emission factor written 0.069 t/GJ (energy) vs 0.69 t/t (per lime) - different bases, not a typo.
